$comment: Non-secret runtime configuration. Safe to commit and to review in a diff.
Every secret lives in .env / GitHub Actions secrets - never here.
The workflow cron fires every 3 hours; this file decides whether a given
firing does real work, so the cadence changes without touching any YAML.

The workflow fires every 3 hours and every firing does real work, all year round. There is no seasonal calendar to maintain, and a discount appearing on an ordinary weekday is picked up within hours rather than within a day.

min_interval_hours only guards against doing the same work twice, from a duplicated firing or a manual dispatch landing beside a scheduled one. Keep it equal to the cron interval in .github/workflows/tracker.yml.
A deal reaches the shortlist when the current Steam price is at or below the historical Steam low. Comparisons run on integer minor units, never floats.

require_new_record then narrows that shortlist to sales that BEAT every earlier price. A game returning to a record set by an earlier sale stays silent. This makes alerts much rarer on purpose: Steam tends to repeat a title's deepest discount, so a game can sit at its all-time low again and again without ever going lower. Set it to false to hear about those too.
Wording shown on the phone. Kept out of the source so it can be any language. The only placeholder is {count}.

record_marker prefixes games whose sale beat every earlier price. It is empty by default because require_new_record is on, so every reported game is already a record and the marker would be noise. Set it to something like "🔥 " if you turn that rule off.

state.$comment: Entries older than this are purged so the state file cannot grow without bound.
